claims.text: The controlled starting material is homogenized, single-phase, polycrystalline HfNbTaTiZr.
Thermally activated dislocation slip becomes significant in HfNbTaTiZr at elevated temperatures.
Short-range atomic reordering becomes significant in HfNbTaTiZr at elevated temperatures.
Increasing temperature activates otherwise dormant dislocation slip systems and increases dislocation mobility.
Elevated temperature promotes local atomic rearrangements in HfNbTaTiZr.
Dislocation activation and short-range ordering alter microstructural barriers to deformation.
Thermally induced dislocation activity and atomic reordering reduce the alloy's effective elastic modulus.
Local atomic rearrangements increase atomic-spacing variability.
Increased atomic-spacing variability produces a higher thermal expansion coefficient.
Elevated-temperature microstructural evolution causes non-linear stress-strain behavior.
Above approximately 500 °C, HfNbTaTiZr should show a measurable decrease in elastic modulus relative to measurements below 300 °C.
Above approximately 500 °C, HfNbTaTiZr should show a more non-linear stress-strain response than below 300 °C.
Above approximately 500 °C, HfNbTaTiZr should show a higher thermal expansion coefficient than below 300 °C.
Below 300 °C, thermally activated dislocation movement and atomic reordering are minimal.
The proposed responses should hold at strain rates below 10^(-3) s^(-1), where thermal activation is not suppressed.
The proposed responses should hold up to approximately 1000 °C provided no phase instability or decomposition occurs.
Rapid loading or temperatures that induce additional phenomena may invalidate the proposed mechanism.
